title: Trump gives Russia 50 days to reach a deal and announces NATO-funded weapons for Ukraine
body:
On 14 July 2025, US President Donald Trump announced in the Oval Office, alongside NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, that he would impose tariffs if no deal to end the war in Ukraine was reached within 50 days. He called them "secondary tariffs," aimed at Russia's trading partners. He said, "We're going to be doing very severe tariffs if we don't have a deal in 50 days," and added, "I use trade for a lot of things. But it's great for settling wars." The Associated Press report did not give a tariff rate.

Trump and Rutte also described an arrangement under which European allies would buy US military equipment and transfer it to Ukraine. Rutte named Germany, Finland, Canada, Norway, Sweden, the United Kingdom and Denmark as buyers, and said "speed is of the essence here." Trump confirmed that the United States was sending Ukraine more Patriot air defence missiles. Germany offered to finance two Patriot systems, after already giving Ukraine three of its own. Trump said the European Union would pay the United States for the weapons. The AP noted that the EU itself cannot buy weapons under its treaties, although individual member states can and were doing so.

The article did not include an official Kremlin statement. Kirill Dmitriev, Vladimir Putin's envoy for international investment, wrote on Telegram that "constructive dialogue" between Russia and the United States was more effective than "doomed-to-fail attempts at pressure."
